<!--
A benchmark is a full revision of a stock assessment, carried out at a workshop on a
three-to-five-year cycle and reviewed by invited external experts. It is not an annual
assessment: the question is not "what is the state of the stock" but "is this the right
assessment, and what should replace it".

This file is ONE STOCK CHAPTER. A benchmark report contains an executive summary, an expert
group information table, one numbered chapter per stock, and the annexes — all assembled by
the workshop chair. You write the chapter; the chair assembles the report. See the
academic-benchmark-report skill for the report-level structure.

The section order below follows the ICES benchmark chapter structure (WKBWNG 2026, ICES
Scientific Reports 8:27, https://doi.org/10.17895/ices.pub.32019630). Confirm it against the
workshop's terms of reference before using it: the outline is stable, the details are revised
each round, and an age-structured stock and a biomass-dynamic stock diverge after the data
sections.
-->

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
source(here::here("R", "report_helpers.R"))
```

```{r benchmark-values}
#| include: false
#| eval: false
# Every value the chapter quotes, derived from the model runs being compared. A benchmark
# compares several candidate models, so keep one object per candidate and derive the
# comparison rather than typing it.
```

# {{PROJECT_TITLE}}

<!-- The ICES stock code goes on its own line under the chapter heading, e.g. reg.27.1-2. -->

## Summary

<!--
What the benchmark changed, in one to three paragraphs: the input data that were revised, the
model that was adopted, how the diagnostics compare with the previous assessment, and how the
reference points were recalculated. Name the final accepted run so it can be found again.
-->

## Introduction and stock status

<!--
The assessment history: when the current method was adopted, what has been changed since and
at which meetings, and the stock's current perceived state.
-->

## Key issues with the current assessment

Why the benchmark was called. Tie each issue to the workshop's terms of reference, and say
which sections below address it.
-->

## Stock identity

Sources of landings and discards, species-identification problems, allocation of unidentified
catch, and national data considerations. State what was revised and why the revised series is
preferred. Distinguish landings, catch, and removals.

Each index: the survey behind it, how it was constructed, its diagnostics, and its
retrospective and sensitivity behaviour, ending with the index recommended for the

-->

## Assessment method

### Explorations

<!--
What was tried, INCLUDING what failed: candidate model structures, the diagnostics that
rejected them, and the convergence or estimability problems that made a formulation unusable.
A benchmark that reports only the accepted model is not reviewable.
-->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-candidates
#| tbl-cap: "Table X.1. Candidate assessment models: structure, data used, and the issue each addresses."
#| eval: false
```

The accepted configuration, and its diagnostics: residuals, retrospective, leave-one-out, and

published checklist that the chapter is expected to work through explicitly.
-->

## Software and reproducibility

The model runs were carried out in `r R.version.string` [@rcoreteam]. The report was compiled with Quarto [@quarto] and rendered by knitr [@knitr], and is reproducible from the model output and the input data.

This chapter and the associated analyses were created with researcher-supervised generative AI (<!-- MODEL -->). The authors specified and checked the analyses, and reviewed, edited, and approved all AI-assisted content, for which they take full responsibility.
